title: In Hinglish, every bell line and closed-app browser alert still comes in English
what: The server writes each alert line in English (a member question, a message, a join request, a free trial, low AI credits, a shop order and the rest). The admin app shows that line as it came: it only rewrites two old English lines into newer English and never translates. So a gym that runs the admin app in Hinglish reads Hinglish screens but English lines in the bell, on Today and in the browser alerts that pop up with the app closed.
expected: Alert lines and browser alerts follow the language the admin app is set to, or the server sends the kind and names so the app can write the line in Hinglish.
who: owners and staff who use Hinglish
fix_line: Let the admin app write each alert line in the chosen language from the alert kind and names

title: Two alert words are not quite true: credit alerts are titled news from your members, and the at-once list leaves some out
what: 1) When the gym runs low on AI credits, or members use up the month of AI answers, the browser alert arrives titled "MettleUp: news from your members", though it is about the gym's own credits. 2) The alert settings say which alerts "always come at once": complaints, shop orders, the check-in poster, a friend who wants to join and a pause or renew request near the plan end. The server also sends at once every online join request, every free trial started online and every question from the gym web page, which the list does not name, so an owner who picked a daily summary is surprised by them.
expected: Credit alerts carry a title about credits; the at-once list names every kind the server sends at once.
how_often: each credit alert; each online join or page question
fix_line: Give credit alerts their own title and add the missing kinds to the at-once list
